findings.observation: Production was initially routed to a different manga tool.
findings.rule: Identify FURU before launching. Follow the confirmed app and actual browser capabilities.
findings.reason: Two manga tools can be installed simultaneously.

findings.observation: Truncated log previews and a missing script handoff caused unnecessary questions.
findings.rule: Read the latest full diagnostic JSON and show the whole detailed script before approval, audit and drawing.
findings.reason: The user needs the actual script and diagnostic events before decisions.

findings.observation: A redrawn page needs a single current pair plus restorable earlier files.
findings.rule: Read pageVersions and restore a saved attempt on its explicitly applied page.
findings.reason: This preserves both the image and its own generation context without another generation.

findings.observation: The separate skill included social-sharing consent but the client-facing MCP workflow prompt ended at saving.
findings.rule: After showing all saved pages, honor a choice already made. If undecided, ask once. Provide drafts on request; publication requires specific approval.
findings.reason: Clients using the workflow prompt and clients reading the bundled skill should offer the same final choice.

findings.observation: A change in character voice in the last panel exposed a gap in the pre-presentation workflow.
findings.rule: Compare every page and panel, cover and total, references, voice, dialogue and depiction, causes and payoffs. Fix inconsistencies and present the complete corrected script before visible review or approval.
findings.reason: Basing approval on the fully checked script keeps internal review, visible audit and the user’s actual decision distinct.

findings.observation: A failed release stage and long-running delegated work need a clear owner and a recovery path.
findings.rule: Report a changed state, trace the cause, try an authorized fix, verify the failed step and its successor. Keep independent work moving and avoid duplicate charges or publication.
findings.reason: Users need the actual status and continuation of permitted work without polling the assistant.

findings.observation: A forced line break inside a name can make a small caption or balloon hard to read.
findings.rule: Preserve meaningful groups, proper names, ruby and punctuation in vertical and horizontal lettering. Adjust available space, read the image at publication size and check the adopted PNG, JSON and version history after a local correction.
findings.reason: Legibility is determined by the rendered lettering and its context.

findings.observation: A completed project’s preference for less background detail must not become a default for later stories.
findings.rule: Choose background detail, contrast and focus for the purpose of each panel. Check project settings and final drawing instructions against the rendered page and its reading order.
findings.reason: An establishing view and a close-up serve different narrative purposes.

findings.observation: User specified that natural figures and limbs crossing panel borders are ordinary manga staging choices.
findings.rule: Accept crossings when story, speech ownership, lettering and necessary action remain readable. A boundary crossing alone is not a reason to redraw or impose a page quota.
findings.reason: Legible manga benefits from freedom in framing.

findings.observation: User reported a missing full stop in the last speech balloon and requested the same rule for standalone and multipage manga.
findings.rule: Author completed Japanese statements with 。 and preserve questions and exclamations, including combinations. Regulate speech before approval, leave source labels and mid-sentence breaks untouched, and copy approved lettering verbatim.
findings.reason: Book-page authoring had its own prompt. The old ordinary-page prompt also treated decorative symbols as sentence endings and contradicted the intended editorial rule.

findings.observation: A generated lettering edit inserted extra full stops at column boundaries inside a single sentence.
findings.rule: Read speech across line and column wraps and compare sentence marks in context. Preserve terminal punctuation and its position. Repair only the affected balloon.
findings.reason: The prior native-page transcription comparison discarded punctuation and could miss extra or missing full stops and altered question or exclamation marks.

findings.observation: Column wraps are layout; editing must retain the grammatical position of sentence marks and all approved artwork.
findings.rule: Keep the established native layout template. Localize replacements and verify original punctuation despite line breaks.
findings.reason: The first experimental implementation exceeded compact render and repair budgets; preserve byte-stable source layout and fit the explicit rule into the replacement instructions.
